newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 90,000 T sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 90,000 T sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award up to 90,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender later on Wednesday, traders said.
But it remained unclear which Paris futures contract the Commission would use as a basis to calculate its maximum restitution level, which would in turn affect the tonnage awarded, they said.
"There's been a big debate -- I think a lot of participants will be keen to get licences because there's no point in waiting," said one trader.
"The dollar exchange rate is very favourable this morning and people are somehow expecting the market to bounce," he said, forecasting a tonnage range of between 60,000 and 90,000 tonnes.
The EU's maximum restitution was expected at 46.198 Ecus (European currency units) based on the May contract, he added. If the March contract was used, then the maximum level would be 46.281 Ecus.
In its last tender on January 15, the EU awarded 47,250 tonnes at maximum rebate of 46.302 Ecus.
But another trader said the spot March contract was a more likely basis for the calculation as it closed at a $1.00 discount to May.
"My feeling is that it will be the March because nobody is going to have much interest in putting in (for licences) against the May, especially if it's trading at a premium," he said.
He forecast a range of between 40,000 and 50,000 tonnes for the award, similar to last week.
"I don't think there's that high a demand for licences," he said.
